{{Quote|But during your time away, you must not forget what Dathomir has given you. Although space is cold and empty, Dathomir's wilderness is lush and rich. It may be years before you return, so never forget the place that birthed and nurtured you&mdash;you will always be a Nightsister.|Mother Talzin|<ref name="BookOfSith" />}}
The '''Nightsisters''' were a sect of the [[Witches of Dathomir]] who embraced the usage of [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark arts]] within their [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-driven [[Dathomir Magic|Magics]]. The Nightsisters were originally members of other [[Witch/Legends|witch]] clans who began to utilize the dark side in defiance of the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light-sided]] orthodoxy found in the ''[[Book of Law/Legends|Book of Law]]''&mdash;the governing holy text of the [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomiri]]. These witches adopted a shamanistic culture that rejected the notion of "good" and "evil", and instead chose to call upon the twin energies of the [[Daughter/Legends|Winged Goddess]] and the [[Son/Legends|Fanged God]] in order to utilize their Magicks and communicate with the [[Spirit (Nightsisters)|spirit realm]]. They focused extensively on the art of casting Force [[Mind trick/Legends|illusions]] through "illusion spells." 

Operating under a revised holy text known as the ''[[Book of Shadows]]'', these sorceresses used their powerful connection to Dathomir's untamed wilds to terrorize their fellow clans and fight for dominance over the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. Although the witches had designs for [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] dominance, they were largely confined to their own world, as the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] maintained active [[Interdiction field/Legends|interdiction]] of the planet. The Nightsisters themselves were divided into various competing clans of their own until approximately [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], when [[Clan mother/Legends|Clan mother]] [[Zalem/Legends|Zalem]] attempted to use Dathomir's legendary [[Infinity Gate]] to destroy [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the capital [[Planet/Legends|world]] of the Galactic Republic. After the plot was foiled and Zalem was [[Death/Legends|killed]] by her [[Ros Lai|daughter]], the numerous clans of Nightsisters were united into a single [[Coven/Legends|coven]] by the [[Shaman/Legends|shaman]] Mother [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]]. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Nightsisters came to the forefront of galactic notoriety when Talzin transformed her people into a [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] society that trained in combat and Magick so that their services as [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]], [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]], and [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] could be sold to off-world bidders.

The time of relative prosperity would come to an end when the clan was drawn into the Clone Wars after Talzin's failed assassination attempt on [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] with former Sister [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]]. Sending [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] and a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] army to Dathomir, Dooku assaulted the Nightsisters' [[Nightsister fortress|Fortress]]. The ensuing [[Battle of Dathomir/Legends|battle]] resulted in the near-extermination of the Nightsisters, though enough survivors remained for the Nightsisters to eventually resume their dominant position in Dathomir's affairs after the survivors were reunited by [[Gethzerion]].

During the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] maintained a significant presence on Dathomir, but after the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] and [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] came to understand the depths of the Nightsisters new leader, Gethzerion, he resumed the Jedi's former quarantine of the planet in an attempt to ensure that none of the witches escaped off-world. Despite Palpatine's efforts, many of the Nightsisters were able to flee Dathomir by allying with the criminal [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]]. In the final [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the Emperor's reign, Dathomir was placed under the command of [[Zsinj]], an Imperial [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]] who declared himself a [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] after Palpatine's death in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. Zsinj maintained the Emperor's forced isolation of Dathomir until [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], when Gethzerion and her Nightsisters succeeded in capturing [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Han Solo/Legends|General Han Solo]] on the planet's surface. The Clan Mother brokered a deal with the Imperial Warlord to trade General Solo for interstellar [[Transport/Legends|transport]], but reneged on the arrangement and attempted to flee Dathomir without Zsinj's blessing. In retaliation, Zsinj directed his forces to destroy Gethzerion's transport, thereby killing her and all the Nightsisters aboard. This betrayal fragmented the Nightsisters, however the witches were able to reorganize by around [[23 ABY/Legends|23 ABY]], when [[Tamith Kai]] and her new Nightsisters allied with the [[Second Imperium]] faction of the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]]. The clan survived through the [[Second Galactic Civil War]] and in [[43 ABY|43.5 ABY]], briefly allied with a [[Lost Tribe of Sith|Lost Tribe]] of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith Order]] against the [[New Jedi Order]].

==History==
{{Quote|The Nightsisters are their Sith.|Han Solo, explaining the relationship between Nightsisters and Dathomiri Witches|<ref name="Backlash" />}}
===Founding===
{{Quote|We divided into clans, and for a long time the clans vied for men in friendly competition, stealing mates. We governed ourselves, punished anyone caught using the night spells.|Teneniel Djo|<ref name="CoPL" />}}
[[File:Nightsister_Initiate.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A Nightsister Initiate.]]
The female [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-users]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] traced their roots back to [[Mother (title)/Legends|Mother]] [[Allya/Legends|Allya]], a rogue [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] who had been sentenced to exile on that [[Prison/Legends|penitentiary colony]] around [[600 BBY/Legends|600 BBY]].<ref name="NEC" /> After using her powers to subjugate the other exiles, Allya showed the first Dathomirian women how to use the Force, managing to create her own sect of all-female Force users. Concerned with regulating her new community's social life, Allya wrote the ''[[Book of Law/Legends|Book of Law]]'', which she based on the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]].<ref name="JVS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>

Over the ensuing centuries, the [[Witches of Dathomir]]&mdash;also known as "Daughters of Allya"&mdash;divided into different clans or [[Sister (Witches of Dathomir)|sisterhoods]]. However, some of the Sisters let themselves drown in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]], just like Allya herself before she was redeemed. As a consequence, the Witches of Dathomir instated a tradition of exiling [[darksider]]s and others who broke their ancient code to live outside their clans in solitude and contemplation.<ref name="CoPL" />

However, at some point during the last few centuries of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], while [[Allaya Djo]] was the warmaster of the [[Singing Mountain Clan]], two Sisters named [[Gethzerion]] and [[Baritha]] were exiled after attempting to [[Death/Legends|assassinate]] their leader, [[Augwynne Djo]] (who was also Gethzerion's birth mother). They banded together with other outcasts to form a new clan, which became known as the Nightsisters&mdash;as they studied the forbidden "night spells." Over time, this group came to resemble the traditional clans and started to expand, raising its own children to obey the power of the dark side, although they did not regard it in those terms. While the other clans refused to forcibly oppose them, their numbers rose steadily.<ref name="CoPL" />

The self-proclaimed Mother Gethzerion even provided her flock with the ''[[Book of Shadows]]'', an instructional treatise on the Nightsisters' new sinister spells and rituals.<ref name="CrackenTD">''[[Cracken's Threat Dossier]]''</ref> As years went by, this initial group of exiles divided into multiple [[Coven/Legends|covens]], which quickly started competing for food, land domination, male slaves and magical supremacy.<ref name="Infinity'sEnd">''[[Star Wars: Infinity's End]]''</ref>

===Rise of the Dathomirians===
Several centuries prior to the fall of the Republic, a band of [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] came to Dathomir with a shipment of male [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]], a [[Species/Legends|species]] of horned [[Near-Human]]s. The all-Human Nightsisters took interest in those newcomers and discovered that they were genetically compatible. The interbreeding of Humans and Zabraks resulted in the emergence of a [[Hybrid/Legends|hybrid]] race known as the [[Dathomirian/Legends|Dathomirians]].<ref name="EYAWtKAtNbWAtA">{{InsiderCite|122|Everything You Always Wanted to Know about the Nightsisters but Were Afraid to Ask}}</ref> The girls were integrated into the covens, while the boys, known as the [[Nightbrothers/Legends|Nightbrothers]], were kept as slaves and breeders.<ref name="BookOfSith" /> From this period on, the Nightsister clans' population was made up of both full Humans and Dathomirian hybrids.

===Queen Zalem's ambition===
{{Quote|Now, Sisters, with the help of our blue friend here, I will reset the coordinates&hellip; so the Infinity wave will be directed at the heart of our enemies&hellip; Coruscant!|Queen Zalem|<ref name="Infinity'sEnd" />}}
[[File:Zalem_walks.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Zalem, Nightsister Queen of Dathomir.]]
The Nightsisters remained divided into various competing covens until [[31 BBY/Legends|31 BBY]],<ref name="Star Wars: The Comics Companion">''[[Star Wars: The Comics Companion]]''</ref> when [[Clan mother/Legends|Clan mother]] [[Zalem/Legends|Zalem]] anointed herself "[[Queen/Legends|Queen]] of Dathomir". An ambitious matriarch, Zalem had learned a higher mastery of the Force by capturing a [[Ros Lai's father|Jedi Knight]] on Dathomir and forcing him to become her mate. After learning everything she could from the Jedi and [[Reproduction/Legends|siring]] a daughter named [[Ros Lai]], Zalem had killed her male slave. Now strong in the Force, she rediscovered Dathomir's legendary and forgotten [[Star Temple]]s, a series of mysterious pyramids built by the long-lost [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]] civilization. Zalem successfully unlocked the secrets of the pyramids and discovered the [[Infinity Gate]]s, powerful artifacts that could project devastating [[Infinity Wave|energy waves]] capable of sucking entire planets into infinity. Haunted with ambition, Zalem hatched a plot to destroy [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the capital world of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], with the help of those ancient Kwa. However, the self-appointed queen's plan for galactic domination was [[Mission to Dathomir (Post–Naboo crisis)|foiled]] by the Jedi Knight [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]], with the help of Zalem's own daughter. Ros Lai stabbed her mother in the [[Breast/Legends|chest]] with a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], ending her reign over the united Sisters. While the other witches expected her to take the mantle of Queen, Ros Lai was taken into custody on Coruscant by Vos, therefore ending Zalem's lineage.<ref name="Infinity'sEnd" />

Following Zalem's failure, a new authority figure arose. [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]], who was both Clan Mother and shaman of her coven, succeeded in reuniting the competing clans under her banner. Under Talzin, the Nightsisters entered into a prosperous era.<ref name="EYAWtKAtNbWAtA" /> At that time, Mother Talzin decreed that the Sisters under her lead could only mate with Zabrak Nightbrothers. Talzin also established a clear policy of separation, with the Brothers staying aloof from the Sisters.<ref name="BookOfSith" />

===Clone Wars===
{{Quote|We could certainly use the power of the Nightsisters against the Jedi.|Count Dooku, speaking to Nightsister Talzin|<ref name="M" />}}
[[File:DaughtersOfDathomir-TSWB.png|thumb|left|300px|Nightsisters during the Clone Wars.]]
In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the Galactic Republic went to war against the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. At some point during that pan-galactic conflict, a group of Nightsisters came into contact with the [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] and leader of the Confederacy. That sisterhood were under the control of [[Sai Sircu]] and [[Yansu Grjak]]. Dooku recruited them into the Confederacy to help with [[Spy/Legends|espionage]], but their true goals were their own.<ref name="Ns1">{{SWArchive|url=games/videogames/news20081009.html|text=Nightsisters and ''The Clone Wars''}}</ref> They were involved in the plot to smuggle and make use of lightsaber [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]] for a Separatist [[Devastation|superweapon]] which made the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] aware of this new threat. They eventually betrayed Dooku and his [[Palpatine/Legends|mysterious master]] in part to prevent Dathomir's destruction.<ref name="JediAlliance" />

Later during the war, the Nightsisters welcomed back and helped their estranged sister [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] in her quest for vengeance against Count Dooku, who had betrayed her. Two other Nightsisters went with her to [[Serenno/Legends|Serenno]], bent on assassinating the Count. When their [[Mission to Serenno (Nightsisters)/Legends|attempt]] failed, Mother Talzin provided Dooku with an apprentice following the apparent "death" of Asajj Ventress. The Nightbrother [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]] was presented to the Count by Talzin in person.<ref name="CME">{{SWArchive|url=fans/events/jon_stewart_george_lucas_main_event/index.html|text=''Star Wars'' Celebration Main Event: Play by Play}}</ref> Around this time, they also discussed using her Nightsisters against the Jedi in the Separatist war effort.<ref name="CVP">{{SW|url=video/the-clone-wars-celebration-v-trailer|text=The Clone Wars Celebration V Preview}}</ref>

The Nightsisters subsequently [[Battle of Dathomir/Legends|came under attack]] from General [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], who was ordered to wipe them out. The resulting battle ended with a CIS victory that essentially amounted to genocide, Ventress and Talzin being the only survivors.<ref name="Massacre">{{TCW|Massacre}}</ref> Despite enduring heavy losses and greatly reduced numbers, the Nightsisters' presence on Dathomir would never be completely eliminated and the eradication of most of the Dathomirians led to the original human Nightsisters restored to their former prominence. Indeed, by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Nightsisters were re-organized back into a single coven once again under the iron fist of Gethzerion.<ref name="CoPL" />

===Fall of the Nightsisters===
{{Quote|I believe the Emperor himself was afraid of the Nightsisters. That's why he interdicted this planet. Years ago, he started a nice little penal colony here, not knowing about the Nightsisters. When he learned about them, he blew the planet's airfield from orbit and stranded hundreds of his own people here, along with the prisoners, rather than risk letting Gethzerion escape.|[[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], to [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="CoPL" />}}
[[File:Spiderclan_Acolyte.jpg|thumb|right|180px|A member of the Nightsister [[Spiderclan/Legends|Spiderclan]].]]
Around the time of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] established a [[Dathomir Imperial Prison|prison]] colony on Dathomir.<ref name="GatORW">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> Gethzerion and her Nightsisters aided them, tracking down escapees and renegades who hoped to obtain passage off world.<ref name="CoPL" /> Using the dark side of the Force, the Nightsisters began to [[Mind trick/Legends#Force corrupt|corrupt]] the Imperial troops and progressively usurped control of the prison staff from Imperial officers. When the Empire discovered the situation, the Nightsisters turned Imperial troops against their officers. A [[Invasion of Dathomir|battle]] therefore erupted on Dathomir between loyal Imperial forces and the Nightsisters backed by their Imperial [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]]. Eventually, the Nightsisters were defeated and repelled from the prison.<ref name="Insider">{{InsiderCite|65|Who's Who in Star Wars Galaxies|Who's Who in ''Star Wars'' Galaxies}}</ref> When [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine came to learn the true extent of Gethzerion's dark power, however, he began to fear the formidable threat she posed to him. He had all the ships stationed on Dathomir destroyed and detached a fleet group to enforce a [[Blockade of Dathomir|quarantine]] on the planet in order to keep Gethzerion and her clans grounded.<ref name="CoPL" /> The prison and all Imperial forces at the surface were abandoned.<ref name="GatORW" /> These troops continued to fight the Nightsisters for years,<ref name="Insider" /> but Gethzerion and her minions eventually took over the Imperial prison, and enslaved all the stranded Imperials stationed there, trying but failing to cobble together an escape craft.<ref name="CoPL" />

Despite this, there were several Nightsisters, such as [[Silri]], who apparently managed to escape this fate. They allied themselves with [[Tyber Zann]] of the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]]. The Nightsisters fought on the side of the Zann Consortium riding mighty [[Rancor/Legends|rancors]].<ref name="EaW:FoC" /> Other escapees included [[Charal]], who ended up on [[Endor/Legends|Endor]].<ref name="EBFE">''[[Ewoks: The Battle for Endor]]''</ref>

In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{SWG_timeline}}</ref> the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]][[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] entered into a wager with one of his cousins to collect the most interesting trophy the fastest. One of Jabba's minions, the [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]], therefore recruited a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] to recover a Nightsister shroud on Dathomir for Jabba.<ref name="SWG:NT">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=general|Nightsister Trophy|Tatooine}}</ref>

In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], when a number of the Rebellion's heroes were stranded on Dathomir, Gethzerion made a deal with [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Zsinj]] that in exchange for turning over [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], the Nightsisters would get access to a ship so they could escape the planet. However, Zsinj double-crossed them and had two [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyers]] fire upon their escape shuttle, killing them all.<ref name="CoPL" />

===Rebirth===
{{Quote|They are not Nightsisters as you and I knew them. Not wizened crones with discolored skin, who rotted from the nightspells they spoke. No, they are a newly formed order of Nightsisters, young and fair, and allied with the Empire. Their evil is subtle. They tame and ride rancors as we do. They dress as warriors, if they choose. They are not even all women... but they are the children of darkness. They are dangerous, with new goals. Do not seek them out.|[[Augwynne Djo]]|<ref name="YJKSA">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Shadow Academy]]''</ref>}}
Around [[23 ABY/Legends|23 ABY]], a new clan of Nightsisters was formed by [[Tamith Kai]] in the Great Canyon. This clan accepted males and treated them as equals instead of slaves, as opposite to traditional Dathomiri society. The best of the clan were sent to the [[Shadow Academy]] for more training, with the rest remaining in the Great Canyon. Unlike the traditional Nightsisters, this new clan was heavily influenced by Imperial [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] teachings and drew upon the dark side of the Force as a concept.<ref name="YJKSA" /> The fate of those left behind after the Shadow Academy fell is unknown, although at least one of them, [[Lomi Plo]], later left the planet after the [[Second Imperium]]'s fall.<ref name="SbS">''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''</ref>

In [[43 ABY|43.5 ABY]], a clan of Nightsisters attacked the unification ceremony of the [[Broken Columns Clan]] and the [[Raining Leaves Clan]]. They were repelled by the combined might of the clans with the assistance of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]] and [[Ben Skywalker|Ben]], and [[Vestara Khai]]. Some of the remaining Nightsisters were captured by the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] and were forced to teach them their [[Control web]] technique.<ref name="Backlash" />

==Religion and philosophy==
{{Quote|Never serve the Nightsisters, children. They'll treat you badly, as if you were mere slaves. Their taste is foul, so it is best to crush them. If you cannot crush them, then escape from them, for you can continue to serve the good Witches, and hope to crush the Nightsisters another day.|The rancor [[Tosh (rancor)|Tosh]], in a narrative to his herd-mates|<ref name="JVS" />}}
[[File:Nightsister_GH.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Nightsister sentry.]]

The Nightsisters, like all other Daughters of Allya, attributed the work of the Force as that of the [[Spirit (Nightsisters)|Spirits]], a group of supernatural beings that were thought to inhabit a parallel plane to the mundane world. They had special veneration for the "[[The Ones/Legends|Twin Deities]]," the [[Son/Legends|Fanged God]] and the [[Daughter/Legends|Winged Goddess]], who were thought to bring balance to the universe.<ref name="BookOfSith" />

The nefarious witches used the Force through a series of techniques they called [[Dathomir Magic|Allyan Magic]], having developed their own "night spells" by tapping into the dark side.<ref name="CrackenTD" /> Nightsisters were expert at casting [[Mind trick/Legends|illusions]] through "illusion spells," and it appeared that, like the [[Fallanassi/Legends|Fallanassi]], this was an integral part of the way they used the Force.<ref name="Infinity'sEnd" /><ref name="Massacre" /><ref name="WoDM">''[[The Wrath of Darth Maul]]''</ref><ref name="Restraint">{{StoryCite|story=Restraint|book=Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter}}</ref>

Due to their constant wielding of dark energies, the first Nightsisters tended to display ruptured blood vessels in their bodies, especially around their eyes. Certain Jedi Masters like [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] also believed it was their power to manipulate weather patterns that made their aspect so peculiar.

There was no "uniform" or standard dress for the Nightsisters, and each wore clothing that suited them personally, although most tended towards black robes and cloaks, adorned with tribal jewelry and accessories. Many of them also had unusually pale skin, which might be enhanced by applied tinctures. Nightsisters were known to be able to [[Force weapon|empower]] [[Sword/Legends|swords]] and other simple weapons with the Force, making them unbreakable even to the lightsabers worn by the Jedi and the Sith. Although they typically used more primitive weapons such as swords and spears, some Nightsisters did use lightsabers and other variants. Sister Silri used a [[Lightwhip/Legends|lightwhip]] during the Galactic Civil War, and even Gethzerion herself was known to use a red-bladed lightsaber.

Either due to their affinity to the Force and/or their magic practices, the Nightsisters possessed advanced longevity, with some witches known to have lived more than one to several centuries. These included [[Zalem/Legends|Zalem]], [[Gethzerion]], [[Baritha]], [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]], [[Daka/Legends|Daka]], and [[Charal]].

==Society==
[[File:NightsisterWitch.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A Nightsister summoning Force lightning]]
All the witch clans of Dathomir were matriarchal societies. Each coven was a "sisterhood" composed of Sisters under the guidance of the [[Mother (title)/Legends|Clan Mother]],<ref name="Nightsisters" /><ref name="CoPL" /> and the "[[maleling]]s" were generally disregarded.<ref name="CoPL" /><ref name="Infinity'sEnd" /> However, the Nightsisters of a few clans had male warriors, believing them to be beings who were capable of balancing the [[Gender/Legends|masculine]] and [[Gender/Legends|feminine]] energies of the spirit realm. Despite being considered as skilled fighters, these Brothers were still subservient to the Nightsisters, and were kept in isolation.<ref name="BookOfSith" />

Most Nightsisters were full-[[Blood/Legends|blooded]] Humans,<ref name="atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> but some of their covens consisted entirely of Dathomirians, the result of hybridization between Human witches and male Zabrak from [[Rattatak/Legends|Rattatak]].<ref name="EYAWtKAtNbWAtA" /> However, the Dathomirian racial group was drawn to near-extinction during the Clone Wars, when the General Grievous attacked Dathomir.<ref name="Massacre" /> When heroes of the New Republic visited the planet in 8 ABY, most of the Force witches they encountered were Human.<ref name="CoPL" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Nightsisters were created by ''Star Wars'' author [[Dave Wolverton]] in ''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]'', a [[1994]] novel published by [[Bantam Spectra]].<ref name="CoPL" /> However, the sorceress Charal from the TV-movie ''[[Ewoks: The Battle for Endor]]''<ref name="EBFE" /> was [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] into a Nightsister in ''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]'',<ref name="Illustrated">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> setting the Force witches' first canonical appearance in [[1985]].<ref name="EBFE" />

Wolverton noted in an interview that he sought to create a set of powerful female figures in the ''Star Wars'' universe that had been dominated by men at the time, expressing delight that the concept had been picked up by George Lucas for his Darth Maul backstory.<ref name="dwolver">{{WebCite|url=https://boards.theforce.net/threads/lit-exclusive-dave-wolverton-addresses-fan-criticisms-of-the-courtship-of-princess-leia-more.50024454|text=Lit Exclusive: Dave Wolverton Addresses Fan Criticisms of The Courtship of Princess Leia, & MORE|date=2014-11-17|format=Forum|work=[https://boards.theforce.net TheForce.Net]|archivedate=20190423100607}}</ref>

===Comparison with Wicca===
{{Quote|I came up with the idea that the Nightsisters worshiped twin gods after reading up on paganism and Wicca. The Winged Goddess is loosely based on the principles behind the maid-mother-crone of the Triple Goddess.|Daniel Wallace|<ref name="BOS endnotes">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2012/04/endnotes-for-star-wars-book-of-sith.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: Book of Sith (part 4)}}</ref>}}
[[File:NS_banners.png|thumb|left|250px|The Nightsister banners called ''The Maiden,'' ''The Mother'' and ''The Crone'' echo the neopagan belief in the Triple Goddess.]]
There are multiple points of comparison between the Nightsisters and the [[Wikipedia:Wicca|Wicca]], a [[Wikipedia:Neopaganism|neopagan]] religious system based on witchcraft and polytheism. In an interview with the fan website ''[[TheForce.net]]'', [[Daniel Wallace]], author of the ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]'', explicitly compared the Nightsisters' beliefs with that of Wiccan witches.<ref name="TFN">{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/latestnews/story/Interview_Book_Of_Sith_Author_Dan_Wallace_143459.asp|text=Interview: ''Book Of Sith'' Author Dan Wallace|author=Geller, Eric|date=2013-02-11|work=[[TheForce.net]]|archivedate=20190804060228}}</ref> In his official endnotes for ''Book of Sith'', Wallace also stated he invented the idea that the Nightsisters worshiped the [[The Ones/Legends|Twin Deities]] after reading up on Wicca and other pagan movements. One of the twin gods, the Winged Goddess, was admittedly based<ref name="BOS endnotes" /> on the principles behind the maid-mother-crone of the Triple Goddess&mdash;a triune female deity, a goddess with three distinct manifestations.<ref name="3Goddess">{{WebCite|url=http://books.google.be/books?id=KnJgevpp3DMC&lpg=PP1&dq=mother%20crone%20maiden&hl=fr&pg=PA4#v=onepage&q=mother%20crone%20maiden&f=false|text="Maiden, Mother, Crone&mdash;The Myth and Reality of the Triple Goddess" on Google Books"|archiveurl=https://archive.vn/ufW22}}</ref>

The concept of the Triple Goddess was also implied to be part of the Force witches' culture in the defunct [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|massively multiplayer online roleplaying game]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]''. In the game, players could travel to Dathomir and purchase local hanging banners in three different models called ''The Maiden,'' ''The Mother'' and ''The Crone'' respectively.<ref name="EmpireDivided" />

Additionally, the Nightsisters refer to their assemblies as covens,<ref name="Nightsisters" /> a term that has been associated with sorcery throughout the centuries<ref name="Dict">{{WebCite|url=http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/coven|text=Definition of COVEN|work=Merriam Webster Dictionary|archivedate=20191229182059}}</ref> and is now reused by Wiccans.<ref name="Cov">{{WebCite|url=http://www.beliefnet.com/faiths/pagan-and-earth-based/2002/06/choosing-a-coven.aspx|text=Choosing a Coven|work=beliefnet.com|archivedate=20170805223012}}</ref> Similarly, the laws and spells of the Nightsisters are written in the Book of Shadows,<ref name="CrackenTD" /> the name of which is identical to the real-world [[Wikipedia: Book of Shadows|texts]] containing Wiccan religious instructions.
